meta.title: The Lion and the Mouse
meta.textType: story: a traditional tale told by Teacher Kim

paragraphs: On Thursday, December seventeenth, the Explorers met in the school library after lunch. Teacher Kim sat on a low chair at the front. She held an open picture book with a lion on the page. Lily, Mia, Leo, and May sat on a rug in front of her. "Today I will tell you an old tale about a lion and a mouse," said Teacher Kim. The children were quiet, because they loved stories.

Teacher Kim began the tale. A big lion was the king of the forest. He enjoyed sleeping under a tree in the afternoon. One day, a tiny mouse ran over his nose. The lion woke up, and he was mad. He lifted his big paw above the mouse. The mouse stood still and looked up. "Please let me go," said the mouse. "One day I will help you." The lion laughed, because he thought that a mouse was too small to help a king. Then he gave an order: "Go away, little one!" The mouse ran into a small hole among the roots of the tree.

A few days later, two hunters walked through the forest. They tied the lion with thick ropes, and he could not move. Then the hunters went to roast meat by the river. The lion roared, and it was a frightening sound. The mouse heard a strange noise from far away. He ran through the grass and found the lion on the ground. "I can help you," said the mouse. He sat on a rope and began chewing. The rope was thick, but the mouse's teeth were sharp.

At last, the rope broke, and the lion was free. The lion was amazed. "I laughed at you," he said, "but you are a wonderful friend." "Thank you for helping me." From that day, the lion and the mouse were friends.

Teacher Kim closed the book. "Why did the lion laugh at the mouse?" asked May. "He thought that the mouse was too small," said Mia. "Can a small friend help a big friend?" asked Lily. "But the mouse was good at chewing!" said Leo. "I think that a small friend can be a good friend," he added. Lily nodded. She wrote the title of the tale for the blog. "Helping a friend is always a pleasant thing," said Teacher Kim.

sentences.text: On Thursday, December seventeenth, the Explorers met in the school library after lunch.
Teacher Kim sat on a low chair at the front.
She held an open picture book with a lion on the page.
Lily, Mia, Leo, and May sat on a rug in front of her.
"Today I will tell you an old tale about a lion and a mouse," said Teacher Kim.
The children were quiet, because they loved stories.
Teacher Kim began the tale.
A big lion was the king of the forest.
He enjoyed sleeping under a tree in the afternoon.
One day, a tiny mouse ran over his nose.
The lion woke up, and he was mad.
He lifted his big paw above the mouse.
The mouse stood still and looked up.
"Please let me go," said the mouse.
"One day I will help you."
The lion laughed, because he thought that a mouse was too small to help a king.
Then he gave an order: "Go away, little one!"
The mouse ran into a small hole among the roots of the tree.
A few days later, two hunters walked through the forest.
They tied the lion with thick ropes, and he could not move.
Then the hunters went to roast meat by the river.
The lion roared, and it was a frightening sound.
The mouse heard a strange noise from far away.
He ran through the grass and found the lion on the ground.
"I can help you," said the mouse.
He sat on a rope and began chewing.
The rope was thick, but the mouse's teeth were sharp.
At last, the rope broke, and the lion was free.
The lion was amazed.
"I laughed at you," he said, "but you are a wonderful friend."
"Thank you for helping me."
From that day, the lion and the mouse were friends.
Teacher Kim closed the book.
"Why did the lion laugh at the mouse?" asked May.
"He thought that the mouse was too small," said Mia.
"Can a small friend help a big friend?" asked Lily.
"But the mouse was good at chewing!" said Leo.
"I think that a small friend can be a good friend," he added.
Lily nodded.
She wrote the title of the tale for the blog.
"Helping a friend is always a pleasant thing," said Teacher Kim.
